thread.title: Stock market news: Dow drops as Caterpillar, Nvidia raise China growth fears - Business Insider

author: Gina Heeb
title: Stock market news: Dow drops as Caterpillar, Nvidia raise China growth fears - Business Insider
text:
03:58:54 PM EST Stocks end lower after Caterpillar, Nvidia stoke China growth fears (SPY, SPX, QQQ, DIA, NVDA, CAT, AAPL, TSLA, AMD) Gina Heeb Jan. 28, 2019, 10:12 AM
Brendan McDermid/Reuters
Stocks fell sharply Monday after weaker-than-expected economic data and earnings added to fears about a slowdown in China. Wall Street had rallied Friday after the longest shutdown on record ended. Watch stocks trade in real time here.
Stocks fell Monday as another round of dismal economic data from China added to long-mounting fears about slowing growth in the world's second-largest economy and elsewhere.
China's government said industrial earnings shrank for a second month in December, underscoring weakening factory activity and demand in the country.
Not helping the mood, the industrial bellwether Caterpillar (-9%) reported earnings and guidance that missed analyst estimates and warned of waning Chinese demand. The chipmaker Nvidia (-13%) also cited weakness in China as it lowered its fourth-quarter guidance Monday.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.9%, or about 230 points. The S&P 500 shed 0.8%, and the Nasdaq Composite lost 1.2%.
Wall Street had rallied Friday after the government was reopened for three weeks , with President Donald Trump backing down from his vow to keep one-fourth of federal agencies shuttered until his border wall was funded.
But the deal leaves open the possibility that the government could close again on February 15 if no resolution on border security is reached, raising concerns that another shutdown could continue to damage the economy.
"Parallel to the trade truce with China informally reached in December, the temporary reprieve on the government shutdown announced on Friday afternoon removes immediate risk from the landscape without taking away an overhang of concern for the markets," said John Stoltzfus, the head of investment strategy at Oppenheimer Equity Research.
China's slowdown has put additional focus on high-level trade talks between Washington and Beijing expected to take place Wednesday and Thursday. If no deal is reached by March 2, the Trump administration is scheduled to more than double tariff rates on $200 billion worth of Chinese products.
Offering some relief to investors, the Federal Reserve is expected to leave interest rates unchanged at its two-day policy meeting starting Tuesday. The central bank has signaled flexibility on its rate path for the year, saying in its latest minutes that it could "afford to be patient."
"Markets are now pricing in no rate hikes this year, and Chair Jerome Powell will need to reinforce the accommodative rhetoric at this week's Federal Open Market Committee press conference," said Vincent Heaney, a strategist at UBS Global Wealth Management.
Oil plummeted nearly 3% Monday, with West Texas Intermediate trading at about $52 per barrel and Brent just above $60, even after Axios reported the US plans to sanction Venezuela’s state-run oil company.
Treasury yields edged lower, and the dollar was mostly flat against a basket of peers.
The rest of the week is busy with quarterly corporate earnings and economic data. AMD and Apple report Tuesday, and Tesla reports Wednesday.
"If analyst estimates are missed, we could see the SPX and NDX face some headwinds—just look at what happened to the Dow after Caterpillar’s earnings miss," Chris Larkin, senior vice president of trading at E-trade, said in an email. "We’re seeing traders diversify their holdings between a risk-on and defensive holdings—likely moving with cautious optimism given January’s performance."
Fourth-quarter gross domestic product is scheduled for Wednesday, though that may be delayed due to shutdown-related backlogs at the Commerce Department. The Labor Department is set to release the January employment report on Friday.
